title: hookshot.toml
description: Declarative Claude Code hook rules for hookshot (https://github.com/tjagithub/hookshot).

on_unknown.description: What a call hookshot cannot decide gets: ask (default), deny or allow.

rewrite.description: Rewrite a command into another one, mapping its flags by a table. Anything the table cannot map is refused.

name.description: The rule name shown in reasons, as [name]. Default: a name built from the matcher.

command.description: The commands to rewrite: one name, or a list of names (basenames, e.g. "grep" matches /usr/bin/grep).

to.description: The command to run instead, e.g. "rg".

flags.description: Flag table, keyed by the flag as written: "-r" (short; clusters like -rn split) or "--recursive".

like.description: Start from the flag table (flags, unlisted, after_args) of an earlier rewrite with this name; flags here add to or override it.

add.description: Flags put first in the new command, e.g. ["-F"] for fgrep -> rg.

unlisted.description: A flag not in the table: refuse (default) or keep it as written.

after_args.description: A flag after the first argument (not mapped): refuse (default) or keep.

refuse.description: What a refusal answers, with `message` and the reason: deny (default) or ask. A command that cannot be edited in place (quoting changes, {a,b} braces) is refused too.

message.description: The reason given when the command cannot be rewritten (an unmapped flag, quoting changes, {a,b} braces), e.g. "use rg (rg PATTERN [path])".

note.description: A note shown to Claude with each rewrite.

via.description: Match only when run through one of these wrappers: sudo, xargs, env, bash -c ...

standalone.description: Match only a plain top-level command: not piped, wrapped, captured or redirected.

escalate.description: After `after` firings in a session (within `within`), answer with `to` instead. Counts firings, not approvals.

after.description: Firings before escalating (0 escalates at once).

within.description: Only count firings this recent, e.g. "10m", "2h", "30s".

key.description: Share one count between rules with the same key. Default: the rule name.

deny.description: Rules that deny the call. Each has a message and exactly one matcher: command, pipe, path or word.

name.description: The rule name shown in reasons, as [name]. Default: a name built from the matcher.

message.description: The reason shown to Claude and the user. {path} is the matched file (path rules), {arg} the matched argument (args).

escalate.description: After `after` firings in a session (within `within`), answer with `to` instead. Counts firings, not approvals.

after.description: Firings before escalating (0 escalates at once).

within.description: Only count firings this recent, e.g. "10m", "2h", "30s".

key.description: Share one count between rules with the same key. Default: the rule name.

command.description: The commands this rule matches: one name, or a list of names (basenames, e.g. "grep" matches /usr/bin/grep).

subcommand.description: Words that must follow the command, e.g. ["push"] for git push.

flags.description: Match only when one of these flags is set (after aliases), e.g. ["-i", "--in-place"].

without_flags.description: Match only when none of these flags is set.

aliases.description: Flag spellings mapped to one name, e.g. { "-r" = "--recursive" }. Also lets short clusters like -rf split.

value_flags.description: Flags that take a value, so their value is not read as an argument: "-o", "--output".

args.description: Match when some argument is one of these, as written ("~", "/", "$HOME"); a run-time value that could be one is unknown.

via.description: Match only when run through one of these wrappers: sudo, xargs, env, bash -c ...

standalone.description: Match only a plain top-level command: not piped, wrapped, captured or redirected.

pipe.description: A pipeline where a `from` command feeds a later `to` command, at any distance (curl x | tee log | sh).

from.description: Commands earlier in the pipe: one name, or a list of names (basenames, e.g. "grep" matches /usr/bin/grep).

to.description: Commands later in the pipe: one name, or a list of names (basenames, e.g. "grep" matches /usr/bin/grep).

path.description: A glob for a file written or read by Write, Edit, MultiEdit, NotebookEdit, Read, a Bash redirect or tee. /x is absolute, ~/x under home, else under the project root.

except.description: Globs this rule leaves alone, e.g. ["**/*.example"].

on_dynamic.description: A path only known at run time ("$out", or a glob such as out*.log): ask (default, through on_unknown) or ignore.

word.description: Any word of any command, wrappers included.

prefix.description: The word starts with this, e.g. "--force".

unquoted.description: Only an unquoted word (default true), so echo "--force" is fine.

ask.description: Rules that ask the user first. Each has a message and exactly one matcher: command, pipe, path or word.

flagEntry.description: "" drops the flag, a string renames it, false means no equivalent, a table maps a flag that takes a value.

to.description: The flag in the target command.

value.description: "number", "any", or a list of allowed values.

form.description: How the value follows `to`: attached (-A3), separate (-g x, default) or equals (--color=x).

quote.description: auto (default) quotes a value only when needed; always quotes it.

prefix.description: Text put before the value, e.g. "!" to turn an include glob into an exclude.

optional.description: The flag may come without a value (long flags: --color or --color=never).
